defects.detail: 'through the right attainment of conceit' for sammāmānābhisamayā (penetration/comprehension of conceit) reads as acquiring conceit
'The Chapter on Brahmins.' drops vīsatimo (the twentieth)
'the five causes of deliverance' for pañca nissaraṇiyā dhātuyo (elements of escape)
'the cessation of the self' for sakkāyanirodha (cessation of identity/personality)

reason: All render sections 5-6 and the closing niranusayo passage; T2=T3 identical; T5 has 'attainment of conceit' for mānābhisamayā and drops vīsatimo; T7 calls dhātuyo 'causes' and sakkāya 'the self'; footnote apparatus translated only by T1-T3, not treated as content.

defects.detail: 'Acting in unwholesome ways' for asappāyakiriyā (unsuitable activity) gives it a moral sense

invention.quote: <gloss>impediments or dangers that block the way</gloss>
The manuscripts from Mandalay and Phayre omit this opening phrase.
The Siamese manuscript omits the section starting from "lack of grooming"

reason: All give the ten paripanthā and ten āhārā lists complete and in order matching the source and reference; T1=T2 identical; T4 renders asappāyakiriyā as 'unwholesome'; T5 expands manuscript sigla in a partial footnote margin (typed as added_fact).

'Is it possible to forget?' for 俾也可忘 (he lets me be forgotten)
'You do not reply to me' for 報我不述 drops 不述 (not according to reason)

'Would you not look upon me?' for 寧不我顧 (would he not regard me)

'Would you not look upon me?' for 寧不我顧 (would he not regard me)
'Bao ... read as fan, inverted' misreads the fanqie gloss 報反
'How can I forget?' for 俾也可忘 (he lets me be forgotten)

'Would you rather not even look at me?' for 寧不我顧 (would he not regard me)
'not answered with affection' adds 'with affection' to 不見答
